source_observations: MapHeaderGetScriptTable walks outer records in five-byte steps and stops on a zero tag.
MapHeaderCheckScriptTable reads two 16-bit operands, treats a zero first operand as table termination, advances four bytes to each next condition, and reads a four-byte pointer on a match.
RunScriptCommand dispatches script opcodes through the command table, but these paths do not provide an explicit map-table byte-length bound.
Map script entry points are called by overworld handlers; opcode behavior additionally depends on the command table and its scrcmd handlers.

source_observations: ROM 8-bit and 16-bit bus reads mask addresses into the ROM window and compare the resulting offsets against romSize before loading bytes.

Out-of-range reads follow emulator-specific fallback paths, including logging and synthesized values; this is not evidence that FireRed table pointers are valid or that emulator reads are equivalent to hardware behavior.
The ROM loader and memory state are connected through gba.c and the pinned memory header; no mGBA execution or boundary harness was run for these map-script fixtures.
